analysis.few_microbatches: With 1 microbatch, Megatron still uses `forward_backward_pipelining_without_interleaving`, but there is almost no 1F1B steady state. Rank 0 must finish its forward and send activations before rank 1 can start, then rank 1's backward must return before rank 0 can backward. Theoretical fill/drain bubble is 50.0%. Nsys GPU-idle is only 2.63% because NCCL send/recv wait still shows the GPU as busy. Too few microbatches serialize the two stages.
analysis.more_microbatches: Increasing microbatches (holding global batch=8) fills the pipeline: warmup is still (PP-1) forwards, but a 1F1B steady state appears. Theoretical bubble falls from 50.0% at 1 μb to 11.1% at 8 μb. Throughput moved from 16387 to 20571 tok/s.
analysis.diminishing_returns: Relative tok/s gains between successive doubling of microbatches: 1→2 21.83%, 2→4 6.11%, 4→8 -2.89%. Diminishing returns begin at 8 microbatches (<5% additional gain).
analysis.throughput_or_memory: PP=2 improves throughput to 21183 tok/s from PP=1 16198 tok/s (1.308x, 65.4% of ideal 2x). Per-GPU VRAM drops from 41804 to 15468 MiB, so PP still also helps memory capacity.
analysis.pipeline_dtype: Compute is BF16 autocast. Pipeline send/recv uses FP32 because BF16 pipeline_dtype produced all-NaN last-stage losses with FP32 parameters.
analysis.embeddings: PP=2 uses untied embeddings/output weights to avoid embedding-group all-reduce overlapping 1F1B P2P.

primary_bottleneck: Remaining pipeline idle plus activation P2P. The 355.9M model is small enough that layer compute per stage is only moderately larger than send/recv.
